stem:
The diagram shows square P of side 2 cm and square Q of side 4 cm. The side length is multiplied by 2 from P to Q.

Which statement about the area is correct?

options.text: The area of Q is 4 times the area of P, because area scales with the square of the side factor.
The area of Q is 2 times the area of P, matching the side factor.
The perimeter becomes 4 times as large, and that same factor rule applies to area.
The area stays the same because both figures are still squares.

teacher.key_rationale: Side factor 2 gives area factor 2² = 4, so Q has 4 times P's area (4 cm² to 16 cm²). Matching area to the side factor omits the squaring. Applying a perimeter story to area over-scopes. Saying area is unchanged grabs that both are squares.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote right-triangle source into two squares with sides 2 cm and 4 cm; stem refers to the diagram.
